entries.reason: Real-ConPTY writer-block precondition is parallel-load sensitive: it holds deterministically when the test runs in isolation but the 65,536-byte write can drain before the detection window under the full parallel cargo test --lib run. The teardown behavior under test is sound; only the setup precondition is timing fragile, and it is a real platform boundary that cannot be simulated under automated parallel load. The frozen plan routes real-ConPTY behavior to the manual Windows matrix (section 14 acceptance item 10, section 15).
entries.resolution: Run manually in isolation with `cargo test --lib real_blocked_conpty_writer_is_unblocked_by_session_teardown -- --ignored --test-threads=1` as part of the manual Windows ConPTY matrix.

entries.reason: #1063 Stage D-owned exact ignored CLI-member cross-process lock-order CHILD HELPER. A Stage E (#1064) parent spawns it by its frozen fully-qualified name via current_exe --exact --ignored; it no-ops with no guard and no mutation unless the child-mode action, per-spawn nonce, and valid control endpoints are all supplied, so it must stay out of the standard cargo test lane (plan section 8.2 line 657, acceptance item 46).
entries.resolution: Stays ignored by design as a spawn-target helper. Exercised by the Stage E cross-process parent and in-process via the driven-path proof AC_STAGE_D_LOCK_ORDER_DRIVE=1 cargo test --lib -- --ignored --test-threads=1 --exact cli::team::tests::cli_member_lock_order_inversion_driver.

entries.reason: #1063 Stage D in-process driven-path proof for the CLI-member lock-order child helper (no current_exe parent; that machinery is Stage E). It mutates process-global env and pins the once-cached config dir, so it no-ops unless AC_STAGE_D_LOCK_ORDER_DRIVE is set and must run in isolation under --test-threads=1; it stays out of the standard cargo test lane.
entries.resolution: Run manually with AC_STAGE_D_LOCK_ORDER_DRIVE=1 cargo test --lib -- --ignored --test-threads=1 --exact cli::team::tests::cli_member_lock_order_inversion_driver.

entries.reason: #1171 reference measurement for the watcher read seam, not a behavior test. It prints the three numbers recorded in the module doc comment (the full read, the unchanged read and the changed read) via println and asserts nothing, so as a standard cargo test lane member it would be a timing gate with no pass criterion and would go flaky under parallel load. The behavior these numbers exist to justify is pinned by the type instead, in an_unchanged_frame_returns_unchanged_and_carries_no_rows (plan section 7.3, acceptance criterion A10).
entries.resolution: Stays ignored by design as a measurement. Re-take the numbers by hand with cargo test --config profile.dev.opt-level=2 --lib read_seam_timing -- --ignored --nocapture and update the module doc comment when the read seam changes.
